summary: Hard. Creating the Google Cloud OAuth client takes under an hour. Letting any Gmail user connect is much harder: almost every useful Gmail scope is restricted, so you need brand verification, scope verification with a demo video, and an annual third-party security assessment (CASA) if your servers handle the data. Start in Testing mode now (up to 100 test users) and submit for verification as early as you can.

oauth_support_claim.text: Google APIs use OAuth 2.0. Google publishes an OpenID discovery document.

difficulty_claim.text: Reading, drafting or modifying mail uses restricted scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify). Those require restricted-scope verification and, if data passes through your servers, an annual security assessment.
difficulty_claim.quote: Apps accessing restricted data from or through a third-party server must undergo an annual security assessment by a Google-approved third party.

claim.text: Composio names Gmail among toolkits with a Composio-managed OAuth app. With it, your users see Composio, not your app, on Google's consent screen.
claim.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.

endpoints.note: Read from Google's live OpenID discovery document on 2026-10-28.

hands_on.text: 30-60 minutes to a working client, plus 1-3 days preparing verification materials
hands_on.note: Estimated from the steps. The verification estimate covers a homepage, privacy policy, domain verification, demo video and scope justifications.

approval_wait.text: Brand verification: minutes (automated) to 2-3 business days. Restricted scopes: several weeks, plus the CASA assessment.
approval_wait.quote: the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete
approval_wait.note: Google also says brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days and that the automated branding check usually finishes in minutes.

fastest_path.text: Keep the app in Testing (up to 100 test users, 7-day refresh tokens), mark it Internal for your own Workspace org, or use Composio's managed Gmail app while you wait.
fastest_path.quote: limited to a hard cap of 100 test users

phases.name: Create the client (self-serve)
phases.summary: Works the same day. Usable only by you and your test users.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project for production, separate from testing
steps.detail: Google recommends separate projects for testing and production. Only the production project goes through verification.
steps.why_human: Requires Google login and accepting Google Cloud terms.
steps.quote: we recommend that you have different projects for testing and production environments

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API and configure Branding
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform > Branding: app name, support email, logo, homepage, privacy policy, authorized domains. Choose External user type unless all users are in your Workspace org.

steps.title: Declare the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Under Data Access, add only the scopes you use. gmail.send is sensitive. gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted. gmail.labels is non-sensitive.
steps.note: An agent can map your planned tool calls to the minimum scopes. A person enters them in the console.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client with Composio's redirect URI
steps.detail: Clients > Create client > Web application. Add the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config, then copy the client ID and secret into Composio.
steps.why_human: Console login. The secret should be handled by a person.
steps.note: Standard console flow. Not walked by the agent because the console redirects to Google sign-in.

steps.title: Add test users
steps.detail: While in Testing, only listed test users (hard cap 100) can authorize, unless you request only openid/email/profile.
steps.quote: Only users explicitly added to the test user allowlist can access the app (limited to a hard cap of 100 test users).

phases.name: Brand verification
phases.summary: Needed for every public app. Fast if your website is ready.

steps.title: Publish a homepage and privacy policy on a domain you own
steps.detail: The homepage must describe the app (not just a login page) and link the privacy policy. The privacy policy must be on the same domain and explain how you use Google user data.
steps.quote: Your homepage can not be only a login page
steps.note: An agent can draft the pages. A person publishes them and approves the legal text.

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
steps.detail: A project Owner or Editor must verify every authorized domain.
steps.why_human: Requires DNS or site access and Google login.

steps.title: Click Verify Branding, then Publish branding
steps.detail: The automated check usually finishes in minutes. If it fails, fix the issues or request manual review.
steps.quote: The automated review usually completes in a few minutes.

phases.name: Restricted-scope verification and CASA
phases.summary: The long pole. Plan for weeks.

steps.title: Write scope justifications
steps.detail: For each scope, explain the user-facing feature and why a narrower scope will not work. A weak justification can get the request rejected.
steps.quote: An explanation why narrower scopes would not work
steps.note: An agent can draft these from your feature list. A person reviews and submits them.

steps.title: Record an unlisted YouTube demo video
steps.detail: Show the full OAuth flow in English, the app name and client ID in the address bar, and each feature that uses each scope. Automation platforms must show how workflows move data.
steps.why_human: Needs a working app and a person recording it.
steps.quote: Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set Visibility as Unlisted.

steps.title: Submit in the Verification Center and answer Trust & Safety emails
steps.detail: Reviews pause while Google waits for your reply. Watch the developer contact and support emails.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes)
steps.detail: An App Defense Alliance assessor reviews your app. You must renew every 12 months, and new restricted scopes may need re-assessment.
steps.why_human: Contract and payment with an assessor. Security questionnaire and scans.
steps.quote: complete a security assessment at least every 12 months

requirements.title: Domain you own, homepage, privacy policy
requirements.detail: Hosted on a verified domain. Play Store or Facebook pages do not count as a homepage.
requirements.quote: The homepage must be hosted on a verified domain you own

requirements.title: Limited Use compliance
requirements.detail: Use Gmail data only for prominent user-facing features. No ads, no selling, and no people reading the data without consent. If data is used for AI model training, the demo must show explicit consent.

requirements.title: Permitted application type
requirements.detail: Restricted Gmail scopes are allowed only for certain app types, mostly productivity uses with a clear user benefit.

gotchas.title: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days
gotchas.detail: An External app in Testing gets refresh tokens that expire in 7 days, so connections break every week until you publish.
gotchas.quote: tokens granted to OAuth clients with a Testing publishing status always expire in 7 days
gotchas.note: Stated on Google's Data Portability docs; seen in search snippet. Google Ads docs say the same.

gotchas.title: Published but unverified is worse than Testing
gotchas.detail: Publishing without verification shows a warning screen and keeps a 100-user cap for sensitive and restricted scopes.
gotchas.quote: a hard cap of 100 total users applies

gotchas.title: gmail.compose is restricted
gotchas.detail: Drafting mail is not a lighter option. Only gmail.send (sensitive) avoids the restricted tier for outbound mail.
gotchas.note: Corrected during spot-check: commonly assumed to be sensitive.

gotchas.title: Workspace admins can still block you
gotchas.detail: Even after verification, a Google Workspace admin can block or limit your app for their domain.
gotchas.quote: A "Verified" status does not override the Google Workspace administrator's settings.

blockers.title: Annual CASA assessment cost
blockers.detail: Required for restricted scopes when data touches your servers. Prices are not published by Google. Third-party posts quote from about $540/year (Tier 2 via one lab) to thousands for Tier 3 or consultancies.
blockers.workaround: Use gmail.send only (sensitive, no CASA) if you only send mail. Keep data client-side. Or use Composio's managed app during early access.
blockers.note: Third-party sources only. Prices vary by assessor and tier.

blockers.title: Rejection for over-broad scopes
blockers.detail: Google directs you to narrower scopes or rejects the request if the justification is weak.
blockers.workaround: Request scopes only for features already built and shown in the video.
blockers.quote: If your justification is deemed insufficient, your app verification request may be rejected.

agent_can: Map planned Gmail features to the narrowest scopes and flag which ones are restricted
Draft scope justifications, privacy policy sections on Google user data, and the demo video script
Check that the homepage and privacy policy links match the consent screen
Read Google's discovery document and confirm endpoints (done: tested 2026-10-28)
human_must: Sign in to Google Cloud Console (the agent was redirected to accounts.google.com)
Verify domain ownership in Search Console (DNS access)
Record and upload the demo video
Sign up for and pay for the CASA assessment, and answer Google's emails

conflicts.positions: Google's restricted-scope docs say 'several weeks'. A Google Merchant API page says verification typically takes 3-5 business days. Forum posts report waits of 4-6 weeks.
conflicts.resolution: The 3-5 day figure is for a different API's sensitive scopes. For Gmail restricted scopes, plan for weeks.

conflicts.positions: Third-party estimates range from about $540/year to $50,000+, and the high figures are disputed.
conflicts.resolution: Get a quote from an authorized lab before planning around any number.

unknowns: Exact CASA tier Google will assign to a given app, and so the cost.
Current median review time; Google publishes no number for restricted scopes.
